subject: Operational compact for EdenWare integration (webhook SLA & oncall)
messages:
From: Aisha Rana <aisha@edenware.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Integration incident: intermittent webhook 503s + escalation request

Hi Neha / Marissa,

We started seeing intermittent 503 responses from Redwood's webhook endpoint for our ingestion pipeline this morning (window: 08:40-09:30 PDT). The failures are rate-limited but correlate with spikes on our side; several payloads were retried and one customer reported duplicated items.

Quick summary:
- Error pattern: 503 (upstream timeout) roughly 0.8% of requests during the spike
- Impact: partial ingestion delay (customer-facing retry loops)
- Affected routes: /v1/webhooks/ingest (primary) and /v1/webhooks/ingest-bulk (failover)

Can we escalate this to a partner-level SLA discussion? Two asks from our side:
1) Provide an oncall escalation path (primary + secondary, PagerDuty or phone) for incidents that touch the webhook surface.
2) Share Redwood's expected RTO/RPO or targeted acknowledgement window for partner webhooks (we need this for our incident notes).

I attached a trimmed log excerpt (webhook-failures-logs.txt) showing timestamps and request ids. We can jump on a quick call if helpful — available Thu-Fri morning PST.

Thanks,
Aisha Rana
Partner PM, EdenWare
Aisha.rana@edenware.io
attachments: [webhook-failures-logs.txt]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rana <aisha@edenware.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Integration incident: intermittent webhook 503s + escalation request

Thanks for the heads up, Aisha — and for the logs. We see the same error pattern on our side (upstream transient timeouts during burst windows).

Short-term (today):
- We've enabled a temporary routing preference to the secondary ingestion pool to reduce retries and duplication risk.
- Can you confirm whether EdenWare is applying any client-side backoff or concurrency caps? That will help us tune the failover window.

Operational asks (for an "operational compact" we can both sign off on):
- Partner oncall contact (primary + backup) with PagerDuty key or phone number.
- Escalation matrix with SLA tiers: P0 (data loss / sustained 5xx spike), P1 (partial failures impacting <10% of traffic), P2 (latency degradations).
- Expected acknowledgment window for P0/P1 incidents from each side (we propose 15m / 1h).
- Agreed runbook for automatic failover and safe-retry guidance (we'll share ours, please share yours).

I attached a first-draft operational compact (proposed-operational-compact.pdf) that captures the above. Can you fill in the contact details and confirm? If you prefer a working session, let's do Friday 09:00-09:30 PDT.

Ben — looping you in to validate the proposed P0 steps and confirm whether we can make the routing change permanent for the high-throughput window.

Neha Kapoor
Partner Success Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
attachments: [proposed-operational-compact.pdf]
From: Aisha Rana <aisha@edenware.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration incident: intermittent webhook 503s + escalation request

Neha — thanks, received.

On our side:
- Primary oncall: DevOps Lead, Jordan Patel (pager: +1 (555) 321-9876, pd: edenware-inc#oncall-primary)
- Backup: SRE, Linh Tran (pager: +1 (555) 321-6543)
- We do apply exponential backoff up to 5 retries; concurrency is capped at 50 simultaneous connections per integration key.

We reviewed the compact and filled contact info in the doc. We agree with the proposed acknowledgment windows (15m for P0, 1h for P1). Friday 09:00 PDT works for a 30m sync — please send a calendar invite.

> From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

EdenWare Integration Team
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Rana <aisha@edenware.io>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Operational compact finalization & next steps (EdenWare)

Marissa / Ben — quick summary and recommended next steps after the partner replied with contacts: 

Summary:
- Partner (EdenWare) reported transient 503s during a traffic spike. They confirmed client-side backoff and concurrency cap (50).
- EdenWare provided oncall PD contacts (primary + backup). They accepted our acknowledgment windows (P0=15m, P1=1h).

Proposed operational compact highlights (attached: escalation-matrix.csv):
- SLOs: Target 99.9% successful 2xx for webhook endpoint outside maintenance windows; P0 declared if 5xx rate >1% sustained for 10m.
- Acknowledgment: P0 15m, P1 1h (both sides).
- Automatic failover: Redwood will route to secondary ingestion pool when 5xx >0.5% for 5m; EdenWare will engage exponential backoff if 503s observed.
- Escalation matrix: Tiered contacts + PD escalation rule; contact details in attached CSV.
- Operational owners: Redwood (Neha -> partner ops), Product (Ben -> change control), Customer Success (Marissa -> customer comms).

Action items:
1) Ben: please create RED-8421 (we discussed) to capture the permanent routing config and monitoring alert thresholds. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-8421
2) Marissa: coordinate the Friday 09:00 PDT readout and send the calendar invite; prepare customer communication if we see more incidents. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345
3) I'll upload the filled compact to DocSend and send to EdenWare for a final signoff (link: https://docsend.com/view/edenware-integration-plan).

Attachments: escalation-matrix.csv (contacts + escalation steps)

Thanks — planning to close the compact this week if we get confirmation on Ben's RED ticket and the calendar invite.

Neha Kapoor
Partner Success Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
